item.title: Collective agreement signed for 155 MCAST employees with improved pay and career paths
item.description: A collective agreement covering 155 MCAST employees was signed at a ceremony overseen by Prime Minister Robert Abela, bringing improvements to working conditions, wages and staff well-being. The agreement covers administrative and senior management roles and is intended to facilitate career advancement, greater access to training and skills development, and improved financial packages. Abela said MCAST plays a central role in the country's next economic leap through vocational and professional education, and that strengthening the college invests in the country's capacity to move forward.

item.title: Appeals court scraps two Sliema hotel permits and sends them back for re-examination
item.description: Two Planning Authority Tribunal decisions on nearby 15-storey hotel projects in Sliema have been revoked by the Appeals Court and returned for reconsideration from scratch, even though one hotel is already operating. Judge Mark Simiana found the tribunal had failed to correctly apply the law when it rejected objectors' request for a suspension of the permit, meaning the permit holder could continue building while the challenge was pending. In the St Vincent Street case, the court said amended plans were ordered as part of the final decision without giving appellants the chance to examine and contest them. The court also noted that revoking a permit after construction has taken place creates an illegal state of affairs that prejudices public order.

item.title: Motorcyclist, 67, grievously injured in Qormi crash
item.description: A 67-year-old man from St Paul's Bay was grievously injured when the Daelim motorcycle he was driving collided with a Toyota Vitz driven by a 29-year-old from Rabat in Triq is-Sebħ, Qormi. The accident was reported at 8am on Wednesday. Police said the motorcyclist was given first aid on site and then rushed to Mater Dei Hospital, where he was certified as having sustained grievous injuries. Police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Man and woman remanded over robbery of elderly woman in San Ġwann
item.description: A man and a woman were remanded in custody over the 12 November robbery of an elderly woman whose wallet was snatched from her hand outside her home on Naxxar Road, San Ġwann. Clifford Garrett, 37, faced charges of aggravated theft, causing slight injuries to the victim, breaching bail conditions and recidivism, while Karen Grech, 47, was charged with harbouring a person against whom an arrest warrant had been issued, making false declarations and breaching bail conditions. Both pleaded not guilty; the victim suffered slight injuries to her hands.

item.title: Maritime industry contributed €999 million to Malta's economy in 2025, study finds
item.description: A study commissioned by the Malta Maritime Forum estimates the sector generated €999.29 million in direct gross value added in 2025, up about 41% from €708.2 million in 2018, with direct employment rising from 8,831 to 13,329 jobs. Port activities accounted for 48% of the sector's direct gross value added. The researchers found the sector's share of the overall economy has nevertheless slipped from around 6% to 4.4% over seven years, and said stronger contribution is needed to meet Malta Vision 2050's ambition of raising it to 7% of GDP.

item.title: Mayors back five-point resolution for stronger local government
item.description: Mayors from Malta and Gozo approved a five-point resolution calling for changes to strengthen local government, including the option for mayors to serve on a full-time basis and greater involvement in decisions on funding allocated to local councils. The Local Councils' Association said mayors face substantial legal and public responsibilities that often extend beyond normal working hours, when government departments are closed. The resolution was adopted at the Association's Annual Mayors' Conference in Gozo on 13 and 14 November, which also covered demographic change, a new app for communication with elected members and the forthcoming waste collection tender.

item.title: 157 km/h is the highest speed caught by Malta's speed cameras this year
item.description: A motorist was caught travelling at 157 km/h on Malta's roads during the first ten months of 2026, almost double the country's maximum general speed limit. Home Affairs and Security Minister Glenn Bedingfield gave the figure in Parliament in reply to a question by PN MP Graziella Galea, who asked for the highest speed recorded by each of the country's speed cameras. According to the minister, the highest speeds captured by individual cameras ranged between 100 km/h and 157 km/h, against a general limit of 80 km/h outside towns and villages and 50 km/h in built-up areas.

item.title: Over 250 residents sign objections to proposed 23-unit Paola development
item.description: The Paola parish collected more than 250 signatures objecting to a proposed 23-unit residential project in the locality's historic core, with a priest, a television host, an author and a former unionist among those backing the campaign. The application PA/07261/26 would replace existing houses and gardens in the Urban Conservation Area with basement garages, maisonettes, apartments, penthouses and a townhouse with a swimming pool. As of Wednesday afternoon over 180 objections had been filed on the Planning Authority website, with the objection deadline falling on Friday.

item.title: MFSA flags three unlicensed financial entities claiming to operate from Malta
item.description: The Malta Financial Services Authority issued warnings against three unauthorised financial entities claiming to operate from Malta, two of which it flagged as potentially dubious schemes carrying a high risk of financial loss. The entities, Malta Global Crypto Bank, Profit Capital FX and Venra Bank, are neither registered companies in Malta nor authorised to provide the banking, payment, investment and cryptocurrency services they advertise. The MFSA said all three claim Maltese addresses although information available to the authority suggests otherwise.

item.title: 'Children are not born with prejudice', Commissioner says after racist video
item.description: The Commissioner for Children called for stronger human rights education a day after a video showed a boy repeatedly hurling racial abuse at a non-European worker on a packed bus, using a racial slur and provoking the man. The Commissioner said children are not born with prejudice and that it is a collective responsibility to ensure they grow up in environments promoting respect, compassion, dignity and inclusion. The video was uploaded by parliamentary secretary for equality Rosianne Cutajar, who condemned the incident.

item.title: Director ordered to pay €38,000 in unpaid wages to former employee
item.description: A company director was ordered to pay more than €38,000 in unpaid wages to a former non-European employee and fined €1,800 after a court found him in breach of an employment contract. The worker, a junior front-end IT developer hired in 2020, said he was owed €53,833 but received only €15,705 over nearly three years, with his salary rising contractually from €16,000 to €23,000 a year. The court found no evidence of an agreement to replace the original contract and noted that forensic handwriting evidence confirmed the signatures of both parties.

item.title: Multigas marks 100 years of industrial gas manufacturing with €4 million nitrogen investment
item.description: Multigas celebrated 100 years of industrial gas manufacturing in Malta at an event at Trident Park in Imrieħel attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg, Economy Minister Silvio Schembri, Energy Minister Miriam Dalli and Opposition leader Alex Borg. The company, which supplies industrial and medical gases to industry, pharmaceuticals and hospitals, announced a €4 million investment to expand its nitrogen production capacity. Borg praised the company's role in securing continuity of medical oxygen supply to the health service.

item.title: 18% of children in the free childcare scheme were non-EU nationals last year
item.description: National Statistics Office figures show 17.7% of the 9,461 children in the free childcare scheme in 2025 were third-country nationals and 8.9% other EU nationals, with 73.4% Maltese. There were 207 registered centres with a licensed capacity of 8,609, 93.2% of them privately owned. The data comes as Budget 2027 measures end free childcare for third-country nationals resident for less than five years, with business groups warning of significant repercussions for operators, employers and workers.

item.title: Sparkasse Bank Malta becomes first local bank to offer crypto custody under MiCA
item.description: Sparkasse Bank Malta has become the first credit institution in Malta to offer crypto-asset custody services under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation. The Sliema-based bank has expanded its existing custody services to include digital assets and the credentials needed to access them, initially limited to selected institutional customers rather than retail investors. The bank said the move was driven by changing customer requirements and growing demand for access to emerging asset classes.

item.title: €1.16 million EU-funded project to restore the Simar wetland
item.description: A €1.16 million Interreg VI-A Italia-Malta project running until February 2029 will focus on restoring the ecological conditions of the Simar Nature Reserve in Xemxija, with about 80% of the budget financed by the European Regional Development Fund. Researchers will monitor water levels and rising salinity threatening the reserve's freshwater and brackish-water habitats, and use scientific models to develop management measures improving habitat conditions and biodiversity.

item.title: Malta's inflation rate eases to 2.3% in October, well below euro area
item.description: Malta's annual inflation rate slipped to 2.3% in October 2026 from 2.4% in September, the National Statistics Office reported. Restaurants and accommodation services recorded the highest annual rate at 3.4%, followed by transport at 3.3%, while information and communication fell 2.5%. The biggest upward contributions came from restaurant services, vegetable prices and air transport, partly offset by cheaper mobile phone services. Malta's HICP rate of 2.3% was about 1.7 percentage points below the 4.01% recorded in the euro area.

item.title: 3,843 domestic violence reports in Malta in 2025, most involving psychological abuse
item.description: A total of 3,843 people reported domestic violence in Malta in 2025, Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said. He reported that 72% of reported cases involved psychological abuse, including controlling behaviour, threats and intimidation, and expressed concern about cases that reached court without consequences for the alleged aggressor. The minister stressed that the figures do not lessen the Malta Police Force's commitment to tackling domestic violence and abuse.

item.title: Yorgen Fenech seeks Chief Justice's recusal from the Caruana Galizia appeal
item.description: Yorgen Fenech's lawyers asked Chief Justice Mark Chetcuti to abstain from hearing the Attorney General's appeal against his acquittal in the 2017 murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, arguing he had already expressed a position on issues central to the defence, including the credibility of the police investigation. The chief justice acknowledged the defence's right to make the request and said he understood the allegations of bias to concern objective rather than subjective impartiality. The prosecution opposed the application, saying no legitimate grounds had been established.

item.title: Repubblika to hold national conference on Malta's constitutional future in December
item.description: Civil society organisation Repubblika will hold a constitutional civic convention at the University of Malta's Valletta Campus on 12 December, brought forward from 13 December, to examine proposals for democratic renewal. Three parallel sessions will cover good governance, the constitution in practice, and democracy, citizenship and the common good, addressing corruption, environmental governance, access to information, protest and disillusionment with political parties. Ahead of the conference the group will hold public meetings, with contributions feeding into the sessions.

item.title: More than 3,300 firearms registered in Malta in ten months
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield told parliament that 3,283 new firearms were registered in Malta between January and 25 October this year, including air guns, answering a question from PN deputy leader Ivan Bartolo. Under the Arms Act, citizens may hold firearms for sport, collection and hunting but not for personal defence, and a licence requires club membership, safety training and periodic renewal.

item.title: Radiologists urge government to back tougher tobacco and nicotine controls
item.description: The Maltese Association of Radiologists and Nuclear Medicine Physicians has called on the government to reconsider its position on tobacco and nicotine control, urging Malta to join the 26 EU member states that have agreed to pursue common measures. The association said higher taxation is one of the most effective tools to discourage young people from smoking and help smokers quit, and warned of conditions such as lung cancer, emphysema and coronary artery disease that are largely preventable but burden patients and the health service.

item.title: Government widens prescribing powers of private family doctors
item.description: Specialists in family medicine in private practice will be able to initiate or renew entitlements for a wider range of medicines under the Government Formulary's "yellow card" Schedule V scheme. The extension covers drugs for mental health, respiratory, cardiovascular, diabetes and rheumatological conditions, and for some asthma medicines also applies to paediatric specialists. Health Minister Ian Borg said the aim was to reduce bureaucracy and treat patients closer to home; the change follows September's widening of investigations private practitioners may order through the public system.

item.title: MDA proposes private traffic officers to end weeks-long delays at construction sites
item.description: The Malta Development Association says a shortage of public traffic officers is leaving authorised construction works waiting for weeks. After discussions with Transport Malta, the developers' lobby proposes engaging suitably trained, licensed and insured private traffic management officers to handle traffic around construction sites when public officers are unavailable, under a clear legal framework with strict safety standards and oversight. It says LESA, Transport Malta and police officers could then concentrate on enforcement and road safety.

item.title: Doctors to begin industrial action on Friday over specialist training recruitment delays
item.description: The Medical Association of Malta has given the government two working days' notice of industrial action starting on Friday 20 November, escalating further on 25 November if a dispute over delayed Basic Specialist Trainee recruitment is unresolved. The union opposes plans to assign Foundation Year doctors to specialist trainee duties without formal appointment, and its directives mean doctors will accept only patient-related calls from nursing and medical staff and will not write letters authorising patients to leave clinical areas to smoke. MAM president Patrick Sammut said the delays had caused financial losses and disrupted doctors' career progression, and the union would keep escalating for as long as the dispute continues.
